sections.overview: Exiliboa placata, the Oaxacan dwarf boa, is the sole described species of its genus and is endemic to Oaxaca, Mexico.
sections.identification: The original paper established it as a distinct genus and species of dwarf boa; the accessible summary sources offer little field-level diagnostic detail.
sections.habitat: Published summaries place it in montane parts of Oaxaca, including the Sierra de Juárez and Sierra Mixe near Totontepec.
sections.diet: The species-specific summaries consulted provide no prey data.
sections.behavior: A field quotation in the Reptile Database describes a specimen lying motionless in rocky soil; broader activity is unknown.
sections.reproduction: A 1992 paper is devoted to descriptive and life-history notes, but its results were not accessible in the sources reviewed.
sections.ecology: Mexico’s 2024 inventory treats it as an endemic species; the reviewed sources provide no direct ecological comparison with another catalogued snake.
sections.conservation: The Mexican inventory confirms that it is endemic to Oaxaca; that distribution note is not itself a current threat assessment.
